CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE, SAN MARINO, CA

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design
Review Committee with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City
Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Howard Brody, Vice-Chair Kevin Cheng, Committee Member Judy
  Johnson-Brody, Committee Member Chris Huang, and Committee Member
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij, Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200
Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Recreation
Department, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address
the Design Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for
feedback from members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited
the site and neighborhood. Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary
approval of a project but rather as a tool in facilitating a project through the Design Review process.
No more than two DRC members may participate in Open Forum discussions. Applications that
have been heard by the DRC may not be discussed during Open Forum.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – JANUARY 2, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 3

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design
Review Committee regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter
at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on
Wednesday, January 16, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 2200 Huntington
Drive, San Marino, California.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the
Planning and Building Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for
further information.

  AGENDA REPORT
TO:  CHAIRMAN AND MEMBERS OF THE
  DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE

FROM:  EVA CHOI, ASSOCIATE PLANNER  Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
DATE:  JANUARY 2, 2019  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC13-71  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  1515 EUSTON RD., (LING/RON LOUIE DESIGNS)  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a first and second story addition and remodel and exterior
modifications to an existing two-story residence.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per CEQA Guidelines
Section 15301(e)(1) - Existing facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

January 2, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
February 18, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 6
Object – 0
No response – 1

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if it
finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The neighborhood comprises of both single and two-story structures, the proposed
  project will maintain its current compatibility with the legal neighborhood as the first and
  second story addition are not visible from Euston Road. The garage expansion with a new bay
   window is modest and does not remove architectural features from the structure. While the
  garage expansion is adjacent to the street, it will minimally alter the existing two-story façade.
  Staff finds the project compatible with the legal neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: New second floor windows provide sufficient setbacks and will not have a direct
  sightline into adjacent structures.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: The addition provides matching roof slope, roof eaves and exterior materials.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Exterior colors and materials will be consistent throughout the structure. The single
  entry door is repurposed from the current double doors; therefore, the design and size are
  appropriate for the structure.
    City of San Marino

TO:  CHAIRMAN AND MEMBERS OF THE

  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
FROM:  CHRISTINE SONG, ASSISTANT PLANNER  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
DATE:  JANUARY 2, 2019  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-64
  2240 ROBLES AVE., (BEIDELMAN/JAMES V. COANE & ASSOCIATES)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a one-story addition and exterior modifications to an existing two-
story residence.

The proposed side yard wood fence and gate are not subject to the Committee’s approval.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

January 2, 2019 – First hearing before DRC
February 8, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 4
Object – 0
No response – 8

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if it
finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE
   Comments: The legal neighborhood predominantly consists of two-story structures in various
  traditional architectural styles. Staff finds that the proposed one-story addition to the existing
  two-story structure would maintain compatibility with the neighborhood, as it does not
  significantly increase the overall massing of the structure. The proposed brick bench in the front
  yard is not a specific feature found elsewhere within the legal neighborhood, however, staff
  would be able to support a condition of approval allowing for a minor adjustment to convert the
  proposed bench into a brick wall instead. There are several properties along the same side of
  Robles Avenue which exhibit a low brick wall element in the front yard.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which balances
  the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous properties with the
  reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property within the restrictions
  of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed addition would not result in compromising the reasonable expectation
  of privacy of adjacent properties. The addition does not result in new windows that would allow
  for extra visibility into the neighbors’ yards.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed addition is designed to match the existing building and will reflect the
  same roof pitch, eave overhangs, and window grid system. The existing porte-cochere will be
  eliminated and replaced with a new covered porch that would reduce the overall canopy in the
  side yard. Staff finds that the proposal is architecturally compatible with the existing building
  and would improve the appearance of the front façade. The addition provides more than a
  sufficient setback from the street and is well-integrated with the existing structure.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: The proposed addition will match all existing materials and colors on the two-story
  structure.
      City of San Marino

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-66  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  1333 WESTHAVEN RD.,  Ben Lundgren, Alternate
  (WEBB/JAMES V. COANE & ASSOCIATES)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a one-story addition and remodel and exterior modifications to an
existing two-story residence.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per CEQA Guidelines
Section 15301(e)(1) - Existing facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

January 2, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
February 18, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 7
Object – 0
No response – 5

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if it
finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The legal neighborhood comprises of mostly two-story structures in traditional
  architectural styles. The existing Colonial Revival structure is compatible with the
   neighborhood and the proposed addition and exterior modifications will not alter the
  compatibility of the structure.

  The material board included an exterior lighting post that staff is unable to locate on the site
  plan. If the Committee desires to approve the project, the approval should explicitly exclude the
  light post in the front yard as it will not be compatible with the legal neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed addition on the first floor will not have privacy impacts on adjacent
  neighbors. Window locations and openings are to remain the same for the second floor.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Staff finds the proposed addition and faux window/balcony above the entry porch
  consistent with the structure itself. However, staff finds the proposed entry door design with
  decorative glass transom and sidelites to be contemporary for the style of the structure and the
  neighborhood. Staff recommends removing the transom and proving glass sidelites that have
  solid raised panel on the bottom 1/4 of the sidelite. The hanging pendant at the entry porch is
  consistent with the style of the structure.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Exterior materials, colors and finishes will be consistent throughout the building.
  Window J on the north elevation is an existing view window without divided lites.
     City of San Marino
  AGENDA REPORT
TO:  CHAIRMAN AND MEMBERS OF THE
  DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE

FROM:  EVA CHOI, ASSOCIATE PLANNER  Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
DATE:  JANUARY 2, 2019  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-83  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  2895 CUMBERLAND RD., (FORTIER/LANSFORD)  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to install a roofing material and color that is not on the City’s pre-approved
roof material list. The proposed product is Tilcor steel shake roofing material in Birch color.

The Design Review Committee had previously approved the Tilcor steel shake material in Birch color
at 2905 Somerset Place. The same material in Weathered Wood color is installed at 765 Winthrop
Road, 1380 Winston Avenue, 1804 Windsor Road, 2240 Roanoke Road, 671 Winston Avenue, 617 S.
Santa Anita Avenue, and 1615 Waverly Road. For structures with steep roof pitches, the Committee
required the use of low ridge profile caps.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per CEQA Guidelines
Section 15301(e)(1) - Existing facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

January 2, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
February 18, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 4
Object – 0
No response – 9

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

In addition to the required findings, the Code allows the DRC to consider the following items when
reviewing a roof material applications: 1. Fire, wind and/or earthquake safety; 2. Structural integrity; 3.
 The extent the roof is exposed to public view or view by neighbors; and 4. The ability of the proposed
roofing material to successfully dispose of rainwater for the particular house.

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if it
finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The neighborhood exhibits different types of roofing materials that include
  composition shingles, natural wood shake, simulated wood shake tiles, and mission clay tiles.
  The orientation of the existing structure follows the curve of the corner lot, which makes the
  single-story portion of the roof very visible from street view. To maintain the structure’
  compatibility with the legal neighborhood, staff finds the material and color appropriate but
  low profile ridge caps must be installed to closely mimic the appearance of natural wood shake.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☐NO ☒ NOT APPLICABLE

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☐NO ☒ NOT APPLICABLE

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Staff finds the Birch color to have similar appearance as the existing wood shake
  material on the structure and the Birch color blends in well with surrounding roofs in various
  shades of dark brown.
